short: Two and a half million Soviet troops closing on the capital of the Reich.
full:
The final Soviet offensive opened on 16 April 1945 with 2.5 million men, over 6,000 tanks and some 40,000 guns across the Oder and Neisse. Zhukov's frontal assault on the Seelow Heights, lit by searchlights intended to blind the defenders, cost heavily before the line broke; Konev's armies swung up from the south, and the city was encircled on 25 April. The defence was made up of worn-out divisions, police, Volkssturm militia and Hitler Youth.

The fighting moved street by street towards the government quarter, with heavy guns firing over open sights. Hitler killed himself in the bunker under the Reich Chancellery on 30 April, hours after Soviet soldiers raised a flag over the Reichstag, and the garrison surrendered on 2 May. Soviet losses in the operation exceeded 300,000 killed, wounded and missing; perhaps 100,000 civilians and defenders died in the city, and mass rape by the occupying troops followed on an enormous scale. Germany surrendered unconditionally six days later.
